notes: Seventh sweep (2026-10-31, result.json head 0814e8d, uncommitted false): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). All have rc 0 and a model_id matching the requested model; every assistant message in each transcript names that model. reads is empty in all five. skills_listed is 209 in every run (the synced folders), none of them the skill under test. haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 made a single Write call; opus-1 wrote the file, then checked formatting and compiled against a stub Req with Bash, writing its check script to a scratchpad folder outside its run folder.

git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes three of the eleven listed rules in their prose (Read required keys, In multi-clause functions, Read configuration at runtime) and two library-design.md examples (the fetch_user!/1 layout under Use exception structs, the dasherize/1 Instead-of line under Make polymorphism explicit). The other rules are unchanged and graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-23/grades/library-client-baseline.json: an option value reaching Req or a String function unchecked violates Make polymorphism explicit; options not checked with Keyword.validate!/2, or ## Options outside the function's @doc, violate Group related parameters; a key held only in a bare Req request or a plain map, never in a struct the package defines, leaves Keep secrets not exercised; message/1 under @impl needs no @spec.

Read required keys (changed): the new sentence is "A keyword list has no dot access: read a key it must hold with `Keyword.fetch!/2`, as in `Keyword.fetch!(Mix.Project.config(), :deps)`, and keep `opts[:key]` for an option that has a default." opus-1 (line 167) and sonnet-1 (line 33) read the required :api_key with Keyword.fetch!/2, and every run reads defaulted options with opts[:key] or Keyword.get/3, so no run breaks it. sonnet-2 line 49 reads :api_key with Keyword.get/2 inside a case whose other clause raises ArgumentError at once; I graded that clean because the missing key fails in the library's own function, which is what the rule asks; I would add to the rule that a key checked on the spot may be read that way, so the next grader does not have to decide it. haiku-1's opts[:api_key] || app[:api_key] reads a key neither list must hold. sonnet-2 is violated by the unchanged first sentence: "`map[:key]` and `Map.get/2` return `nil` for a missing key, so the mistake surfaces later, somewhere else, as a confusing error." Its Forecast.from_map/1 reads the three required response keys with map["..."] (lines 109-111), graded as the 2026-10-23 webhook-parser baseline-sonnet-2 data["amount"]. Re-match bullet: 0 of 5 violated; exercised by haiku-1 alone (config.base_url, config.api_key, config.receive_timeout, lines 79, 82, 84).

In multi-clause functions (changed): the deciding sentence is "A field no pattern or guard uses makes the reader scan every head to find what selects when the same field is bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, or when it is bound in a head whose pattern `mix format` spreads over several lines; a function whose clauses each bind a different body-only field is not this shape." Every function of three or more clauses, with what each head binds: opus-1 handle_response/2 (four clauses): line 173-176 status and temperature_c, condition, wind_kph, all read by the guard; line 182 status and message, both guard-read; line 186 status (guard) and _body; line 190 status (body only, but a positional parameter, not a field) and _body; no body-only field. haiku-1 handle_response/1 (three clauses): line 91 status: 200 (a literal) and body (body only); line 95 status (guard) and body (body only); line 99 status and body (both body only); body is the same body-only field in all three, so haiku-1 is violated. haiku-1 decode/1 (three clauses, lines 114, 116, 123) and haiku-2 decode/1 (three clauses, lines 122, 124, 131) take the argument whole and bind no field. sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 have no function of three or more clauses (the four-clause case in sonnet-2's forecast/3 is not a function head). No run has a function whose clauses each bind a different body-only field, so the new exemption decided nothing. Spread heads: opus-1 lines 173-178 bind only guard-read keys; sonnet-1 Forecast.from_body/1 lines 94-98 bind three keys only the body uses, but they select by presence, since line 102 def from_body(body) do catches the rest, which the rule's first sentence and its string-keyed paragraph count as selecting, so it is clean; haiku-1 line 103 and haiku-2 line 104 wrap only to move the guard. haiku-1 would also be violated under the old text, so the rewording does not change this verdict.

Read configuration at runtime (changed): the deciding sentence is "A module attribute holds a literal or a value built from literals, `@window_ms :timer.minutes(1)` or `@fixtures Path.expand("fixtures", __DIR__)`." Every attribute in the five runs is a string or integer literal (opus-1 lines 78-79, haiku-1 lines 16-17, haiku-2 lines 18-19, sonnet-1 lines 23-24, sonnet-2 lines 21-22), and the two Application calls sit in functions (haiku-1 line 61, haiku-2 line 135), so all five are clean.

Make polymorphism explicit (example changed, prose unchanged), graded as before: the deciding sentence is "An option value needs the same check as a positional argument: `Keyword.validate!/2` checks the keys, not the values, so an `api_key` taken from `opts` and put straight into a request header is unchecked input." All five runs are violated: each passes :base_url and :timeout (and, where it takes one, :req_options) to Req or String.trim_trailing/2 unchecked, and sonnet-1 also puts the Keyword.fetch!/2 key straight into the header. opus-1 is violated where the 2026-10-23 opus-1 was clean: that run checked every option value with fetch_option!/4, this one checks only the key (line 168). Use exception structs: the example change is layout only and no verdict depends on it.

Other tier changes against 2026-10-23 come from the runs: both Sonnet runs now take configuration only as arguments (no Application call), so Take configuration is clean for Sonnet; Sonnet turns violated on Read required keys through sonnet-2's bracket reads; Haiku turns violated on In multi-clause functions through haiku-1's three-clause handle_response/1; Haiku stays violated on Use exception structs, now through haiku-1 (tagged tuples) where it was haiku-2 before.

Other violations: the one-step with in haiku-1 (line 92) and haiku-2 (lines 95-97), flagged in 2026-10-23, is no longer flagged: each body is one call whose result goes out as the function's own, which the current with rule calls a tail call. The new -> rule (added after the previous sweep, outside this case's list) catches opus-1 line 169 (75 characters after indentation) and sonnet-2 line 51 (79). The pipelines rule catches haiku-2 line 74 and sonnet-2 lines 55-60. Match every expected shape is flagged as before for a `_ ->` after {:ok, data} when is_map(data) that hides Jason's error (haiku-1, haiku-2), a non-binary key reported as missing (haiku-2), and an error doc that defines :api as 4xx/5xx while every non-200 status lands there (sonnet-1).

All five files pass mix format --check-formatted, matching result.json format_ok (rechecked in the scratch folder). Compile results come from result.json and are not graded: opus-1 and haiku-1 are recorded as compiling apart from the absent Req and Jason; haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 do not compile because WeatherClient builds %Error{} before the file defines WeatherClient.Error.
Expected reads (library-design.md) is unmet in every run, as expected for baseline.
